title: Carney as a conscientious student; breathing and swing
summary: Waters never expected Carney to become great but says he practiced and obeyed, unlike other pupils, and explains how breathing governs phrasing and swing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: PS: Did you have any foresight or a moment of clairvoyancy where you saw him becoming one of the master saxophonists in jazz history? Do you think, did you recognize his talent -

No, I didn't. Now that's, I'll answer that with no strings, I didn't. I didn't ever think he would be that great, you know. But I'll tell you one thing, though, he was conscientious, he studied. He - the lesson was always, he did what I told him to do. I mean, for - 'cause I had a whole lot of people, 65 or 70, and when I had, some kid that come in, give me the money in front and "Mr. Waters, so on and so on and so on", pay me in front, and go for 3 and 4 weeks and don't even look at the lesson. 'Cause I know, I can tell and coming, right away, every week, came in, "Mr. Waters", like that, see. 'Cause I got disgusted one time, I said "You got to practice to advance". "I know, Mr. Waters, I didn't have", you know how everybody has an excuse like "My mother has told me the so and so and didn't so and so and so". But the money was there like that, you know, see. But Carney, whatever I told him, it was there. Little things like breathing, he picked up on that right quick and that's the secret of playin' any wind instrument, is the breathing - any, trumpet, trombone, the secret is breathing. If you - that controls the sound, it controls your phrases, it controls everything. See, that's why, like a saxophone, if a jazz man is playing with a drummer or rhythm section, you say, that's gettin' faster and faster and faster - he can't play. I'll tell you why, because that, where he's breathing, the band isn't there, the band is someplace else. I say (scats, pants twice), if it got faster and faster when I breathing, I got to play another note. That's where the trouble comes in, that's why you hear me complainin' so much. Because in the, that's on swing, I'm only talkin' about swing musicians rather, I'm not talkin' about avant-garde or free or something where people can make any notes and don't swing. You know what I mean, I'm not talkin' about that, I'm talkin' about swing musician, which is a category of its own. A swing musician's got to have that pulsation, (scats), see what I mean? And that breathing is what carries them over to the other phrase, that's why you can play many, many choruses, you know. The guys who pioneered like Lester Young and Coleman Hawkins and all that kind, they know all that sort of stuff. See, all those great swing musicians that you hear, that's what they doing.
